Each is an oval depression nearly a meter long, shallow at one end and sharply cut at the other, spaced at irregular intervals. Water is already softening their edges. They do not lead toward the stack.

Farther on, the birds become louder. The basalt rises ahead in black vertical columns, with a narrow lee on its landward side where the wind drops almost completely.
places.name: across the shining flats

places.description:
The shore tightens beneath the cliffs until the sea-polished stones are only a few dozen paces wide. Moss hangs in dark green sheets from the rock above, interrupted by ribbons of water that descend without drama, some clear and narrow, some broken into mist before they reach the beach.

Here the wind is intermittent. Between gusts, individual sounds separate: water ticking into stone basins, pebbles shifting under the wash, the dry scrape of a bird somewhere overhead. The cliff face is full of shallow recesses and darker seams. Most are only shadows. One, behind the third waterfall, seems to continue farther than the light reaches.

The stones near that fall are unusually pale, almost bone-colored, and a shallow runnel leads from the cave mouth toward the sea. Nothing has been arranged. Nothing points inward. It merely remains possible to go there.
places.name: beneath the falling water

places.description:
Beyond the cobble field the ground turns abruptly soft. Pale sand lifts into long low dunes striped with beach grass, their windward faces smooth and their sheltered sides stippled with tiny tracks. The sea is mostly hidden here; only its sound remains, broad and distant.

Between the dunes are hollows where the air warms a little and the grass stands upright. In one of them, driftwood has gathered around a shallow basin of rainwater darkened by peat. Small yellow flowers grow close to the ground. Farther in, the dunes rise high enough that each crest reveals another set beyond it, and then another.

On the third high ridge, something geometric interrupts the landscape: four weathered stone posts in a rough square, each barely knee-high, with no wall or roof between them. Lichen covers their upper surfaces. From there, a narrow line through the grass continues toward a distant stand of wind-bent trees that cannot be seen from the shore.
places.name: the pale dunes

places.description:
The inland slope is steeper than it appeared from the beach. Black-green grass reaches mid-calf and bends in long synchronized waves under the wind. The sea drops away behind until the tidal flats become bands of silver and charcoal and the basalt stack looks small again.

At the saddle between the hills the wind changes direction. Beyond is a shallow upland basin invisible from the shore, holding a dark freshwater lake no more than half a mile across. Its surface is smooth despite the moving air. Low juniper and heather gather along the banks.

There is no building, road, fence, or boat. Near the western shore, however, a single line of flat stones extends into the water at walking intervals, each stone just above the surface, continuing much farther than seems useful before ending near the lake's center. From the saddle, another faint path contours around the eastern hill toward higher ground where the coast can no longer be seen.
places.name: the saddle in the black grass

places.description:
The landward side of the basalt stack forms a tall black wall that cuts the wind almost completely. After the exposed flats, the sudden quiet feels architectural. Water drips from ledges high above. The birds are mostly on the seaward face, reduced here to muffled arguments and occasional white feathers turning slowly down through the still air.

At the base of the columns is a strip of coarse shell sand strewn with fragments of blue mussel and pale crab carapace. A narrow cleft splits the basalt at shoulder width. It opens only a few meters in, not into a cave, but into a vertical slot where seawater rises and falls from somewhere beneath the rock. Each pulse arrives several seconds after the sound of the outer surf.

Wedged high in the cleft, far above any ordinary tide line, is a smooth branch of reddish wood thicker than an arm. It is fresh enough to retain bark. No such tree is visible anywhere on the coast.

From the lee, the strange line of broad impressions can still be picked out across the flats. From here their direction is clearer: they cross the shore and continue toward a low reef to the north, exposed only because the water has withdrawn so far.
places.name: in the lee of the stack

places.description:
Passing behind the water is colder than expected. For a few steps the world is reduced to white noise and broken light; then the sound falls away and the recess opens into a shallow cavern whose ceiling slopes downward toward darkness.

The floor is not dry. A clear stream no wider than a hand runs from the back of the cave toward the waterfall, cutting a shallow channel through pale stone. The walls are banded grey, green, and rust-red where minerals have seeped through them. In several places the bands form near-perfect concentric arcs, like sections through trees that never grew.

Twenty meters in, daylight becomes indirect. There is enough to see that the cave forks around a broad pillar of stone. The left branch quickly narrows to nothing. The right carries the little stream and a steady current of air that smells not of sea but of wet leaves.

On the pillar, at about eye level, a small patch of stone has been worn smooth by repeated contact. There is no mark on it, only the polish.
places.name: behind the third waterfall

places.description:
The narrow line through the dune grass descends into a sheltered hollow where the air changes completely. The wind becomes a distant pressure above the canopy. The trees are low, old, and twisted inland, their trunks silver-grey and their branches densely furred with lichen.

The ground beneath them is soft with needles and dry leaves, interrupted by patches of fine white sand. Light arrives green and broken. Somewhere deeper in the grove, water can be heard dripping at a slow regular interval despite there being no visible stream.

The four stone posts on the ridge are not repeated here, but their geometry returns in another form: several trees have grown around rectangular blocks of dark stone, roots gripping corners and disappearing beneath them. The blocks are too regular to be natural and too widely scattered to suggest a wall.

At the far end of the grove, one trunk has fallen across a narrow depression. Beyond it the land drops sharply, and through the branches there is a glimpse of water that cannot be the sea: too dark, too still, and apparently much closer than the coast should be from here.
places.name: among the wind-bent trees

places.description:
The flat stones begin at the western bank and continue one by one into the dark water. Each is broad enough for a careful step, slick at the edges, and set just high enough that the lake laps over them when the surface lifts. From the shore they looked irregular. Up close, their spacing is almost exact.

The farther out you go, the quieter the basin becomes. The wind still combs the grass on the hills, but the water around the stones remains strangely level. Looking down reveals a bottom of pale gravel for the first dozen steps, then darkness. Small silver fish gather beneath the stones and vanish whenever a shadow crosses them.

Near the midpoint, one stone is missing. The gap is wider than the others but still crossable. Beneath it, far below the surface, something catches the light: a pale circular shape larger than the absent stone, perfectly still in the dark.

The final stepping stone ends well short of the lake's center. From there, nothing continues above water. The basin simply opens around you, black and reflective, with the hills mirrored upside down and the sky occupying almost everything else.
places.name: the stones into the lake

places.description:
A narrow door painted such a deep green that it is nearly black in the dimness of the lounge. The paint is old but glossy where shoulders and hands might have brushed it. Its knob is white porcelain veined with a hairline crack; the brass plate beneath has been polished by use and carries no maker's mark.

The door sits slightly deeper in the stone than the others. No light shows around its edges. If a hand rests on the knob for more than a moment, it is faintly warm.

Very close to the lower panel there is sometimes a smell of rain on stone, old wood, and something toasted with butter. It could be coming from elsewhere in the room.
places.name: the dark green door

places.description:
A long covered arcade stretches beneath a roof of iron ribs and old glass, every pane stippled with rain. The storm itself seems to have just passed. Water ticks from gutters into narrow channels along the paving stones, and the whole passage smells of wet limestone, coffee, polished wood, and the faint electrical warmth of lamps.

The buildings on either side are four and five stories high, their lower fronts occupied by small shops with darkened windows and hand-painted signs in an alphabet that looks familiar until read. Above them, apartments show curtains, plants, bookshelves, occasional pools of amber light. No voices carry from within.

A bakery halfway down the arcade is lit. Its front window has fogged from inside, and behind the glass sit several dark loaves, small glazed pastries, and a tray with one empty space. A brass bell hangs over the closed door. Farther on, the arcade opens into a broad square where a clock tower is visible above the roofs, though its face cannot be read from here.

To one side, a narrow lane slopes down between buildings toward the sound of moving water. To the other, a tiled stair climbs toward an upper gallery beneath the glass roof. Behind, the arcade continues around a shallow bend beneath hanging lamps, each one reflected in the wet stone.

There is no urgency anywhere. The rain has finished. The city has not.
places.name: the arcade after rain

places.description:
The lane descends steeply between close-set buildings, its cobbles dark with rain and its gutters still carrying thin streams downhill. Window boxes drip onto striped awnings. Laundry lines cross overhead between upper stories, though nothing hanging from them moves despite the occasional breeze.

At the bottom, the buildings open abruptly onto a canal broad enough for two small boats to pass. The water is black-green and quick beneath the lamps, carrying leaves, reflected windows, and small islands of foam under a low stone bridge.

A narrow quay follows the canal in both directions. One way passes beneath the bridge toward a district of taller buildings where several roofs are crowned with copper domes. The other follows a row of plane trees and old benches toward a distant curve where strings of lights hang across the water.

Moored to an iron ring nearby is a small wooden boat with no name painted on it. Its interior is dry except for a shallow pool of rainwater in the stern. One oar lies across the seats. The second is nowhere obvious.

Across the canal, a single upstairs window is open. A white curtain lifts and falls behind it.
places.name: the lane to the canal

places.description:
The tiled stair climbs between iron railings worn smooth at hand height and emerges onto a narrow gallery running beneath the arcade's glass roof. Up here the rain is closer. Droplets bead on the panes overhead and slide slowly down the sloped glass, catching the amber lamps below.

The gallery passes doors to upper rooms, most closed, some standing slightly ajar. Through one is a reading room with green-shaded lamps and newspapers folded on wooden racks. Through another, only darkness and the faint smell of varnish. Small bridges cross the open space to the opposite side of the arcade at irregular intervals.

Near the middle, the ironwork broadens into a little conservatory suspended above the shops. Tall potted citrus trees stand beneath the glass, leaves glossy from humidity. A round table holds three empty cups and a shallow dish containing six rain-darkened chestnuts.

Beyond the conservatory, a narrow service stair climbs higher toward the roofs. Its door has been propped open with a brick. Cool air moves down from above, carrying the smell of wet tile and chimney smoke.
places.name: the upper gallery

places.description:
The bakery door opens with a small brass bell and a wash of heat carrying butter, yeast, coffee, and orange peel. The room is narrow, tiled in cream and dark green, with a marble counter running along one wall and wooden shelves behind it. Nothing is freshly moving, but nothing looks abandoned either.

Several loaves sit beneath linen cloths. Small pastries glazed with apricot are arranged on a tray beside darker spirals dusted with sugar. One space on the tray is empty. A pot of coffee rests on a black iron warmer, still hot enough to send a faint thread of steam from its spout.

There is no till. A shallow wooden bowl beside the counter contains a few mixed coins, a blue button, two smooth pebbles, and a folded paper star. On the wall above it, a chalkboard bears three lines of writing in the same almost-readable script seen outside. The prices, if that is what they are, change subtly depending on how long one looks.

At the back of the shop, a bead curtain separates the public room from a preparation area. Beyond it are floury worktables, copper pans, and an open transom window looking into a tiny courtyard where rainwater drips from a fig tree into a stone basin.
places.name: the warm bakery

places.description:
The arcade opens onto a square paved in broad pale stones still slick from rain. Arcades continue around three sides beneath upper stories with shuttered windows and narrow balconies. In the center stands a fountain carved as a shallow octagonal basin. Water slips continuously from four bronze mouths and makes a sound much smaller than the space around it.

The clock tower rises from the far side. Up close, its face is stranger than distance suggested: twelve marks around the dial, but no numerals, and two dark hands pointing to positions that would be ordinary if a third, thinner hand were not moving slowly backward.

Cafes line one edge of the square under folded awnings. Tables and chairs remain outside, rain-beaded and empty. On another side, a narrow covered passage leads toward a district of taller houses painted faded rose, ochre, and blue. Between two of them, a flight of broad steps rises toward a terrace where the skyline opens.

Every few minutes, somewhere in the city, a bell sounds once. It does not seem to come from the clock tower.
places.name: the clock square

places.description:
The quay narrows beneath the stone bridge until there is room for only one person beside the canal. The arch traps the sound of water and turns each drip from the masonry into a distinct metallic note. Moss grows thickest where the stone meets the current.

Halfway through, a set of shallow steps descends directly into the canal and vanishes under the surface. They are old, worn concave at the center, and continue visibly for four steps before darkness takes them. An iron handrail follows the wall down into the water.

Beyond the bridge, the canal opens again beside taller buildings faced in pale stone. The copper domes glimpsed from upstream belong to a public bathhouse or something very like one: high arched windows glow with diffuse blue-white light, and steam drifts from roof vents into the cool night.

On the opposite bank, a tram stands motionless at a small platform. Its interior lights are on. No driver is visible. The route plate above the windshield displays a single symbol that resembles a crescent laid on its side.
places.name: under the low bridge

places.description:
The service stair ends at a heavy metal door standing open to the night. Beyond it, the roofs spread in overlapping planes of wet tile, slate, glass, and dark metal. Chimneys breathe pale threads of smoke. Rainwater runs along copper gutters and spills from gargoyles into alleys far below.

Narrow maintenance walks connect several buildings. Some are proper iron bridges with railings; others are boards laid between parapets with an optimism that feels historical rather than current. Pots of rosemary, thyme, and small citrus trees cluster wherever walls shelter them from the wind.

From here the city extends much farther than the arcade implied. Domes, towers, roof gardens, narrow spires, and occasional glasshouses rise in every direction beneath a clearing sky. The clouds have begun to split in the west, revealing a band of deep indigo and, lower still, a line of impossible orange light as though sunset were occurring somewhere beyond midnight.

On the nearest higher roof stands a small pavilion with open sides and a copper roof. A telescope is mounted there, angled not toward the sky but down across the city.
places.name: the roofs after rain

places.description:
The bathhouse entrance is set beneath one of the copper domes, reached by a short bridge over the canal. Inside, the air turns warm and mineral-rich. Blue-white light comes from frosted glass globes and from somewhere beneath the water itself.

The first hall is lined with dark wooden benches, hooks, folded towels, and shallow stone basins. Beyond it opens a chamber large enough to contain several pools separated by low arches. Steam hangs beneath the vaulted ceiling. Some pools are perfectly still; others overflow continuously through carved channels into lower basins.

The stone underfoot is warm. Mosaics cover the walls in muted blue, cream, and black: waves, birds, constellations, boats, hands holding cups. One panel has been repaired with pieces that do not quite match, so that a flock of birds becomes, halfway across the wall, a set of small black stars.

At the far end is an open-air pool beneath the central dome, whose oculus has no glass. Rainwater occasionally falls from the roof edge into the hot water. From the pool, the clearing night sky is visible directly overhead while the city remains hidden beyond the walls.

A narrow passage marked only by three horizontal lines descends farther below the baths. Warm air rises from it in slow breaths.
places.name: the blue bathhouse

places.description:
The pavilion stands on four slender iron posts under a shallow copper roof gone green at the edges. The telescope is longer than it looked from below, mounted on a brass cradle with slow-turning gears and a padded eyepiece. Its tube is painted cream and marked only with a fine black line around the middle.

It cannot be raised high enough to see the sky. The mount permits only a broad sweep across the city below.

Through the eyepiece, distant details become unnervingly intimate: steam feathering from a bathhouse vent, rain trembling on a balcony rail, a page turning by itself in an upstairs room where the window is open. The optics are excellent enough to reveal things that should simply be too small at this distance.

Most strikingly, the telescope does not seem perfectly aligned with ordinary space. Certain roofs visible through it are not visible to the naked eye. A narrow courtyard appears between two buildings that, from the pavilion, plainly touch. A lit room occupies the upper story of a warehouse that has no upper story at all.

Etched into the brass focusing wheel are four tiny words in the almost-readable local script. Staring at them produces the strong impression that one of them means 'near.' The other three refuse to settle.
places.name: the downward telescope

places.description:
A narrow steel door with rounded upper corners, painted a dark enamel blue. Three shallow horizontal ridges cross its lower half. The brass handle is the sort meant to be gripped rather than turned, and the metal around it is worn to a softer shine.

Unlike most of the doors in the lounge, this one never feels entirely still. A hand laid against the panel may detect the faintest continuous vibration, so slight it could be blood in the fingertips.

There is a narrow strip of ribbed glass near the top. It shows only diffuse amber light. Now and then, very close to the seam, the air smells briefly of cold iron, wool upholstery, coffee, and smoke carried from a great distance.
places.name: the narrow blue door

places.description:
A narrow vestibule opens into a train corridor paneled in dark wood and brass. Small amber lamps sway almost imperceptibly overhead. The floor moves with the long, patient rhythm of wheels on rail: a gentle lateral roll, then the faintest lift, then level again.

Tall windows line one side. Beyond them, night country passes at speed beneath a moon obscured by thin cloud. Sometimes there are black fields silvered with frost. Sometimes pine forest. Once, for several seconds, a broad river keeps pace beside the train, reflecting lights that do not seem to belong to any settlement.

The corridor extends in both directions through glass-paneled doors. One way smells faintly of coffee, citrus peel, and hot metal. The other is quieter, lined with compartment doors and heavy blue curtains. Farther down, a warmer gold light suggests a larger carriage.

A brass route frame is mounted to the wall beside the window. It contains a long strip of cream paper printed with station marks and connecting lines, but every station name has been removed cleanly, leaving only dots, distances, and a single small red arrow pointing onward.

The train is moving. Nothing indicates when it began or where it intends to stop.
places.name: between the swaying lamps

places.description:
The dining car is brighter than the corridor but no less quiet. Small shaded lamps stand on white-clothed tables, each pool of light reflected in the dark windows. Brass luggage racks curve overhead. The upholstery is deep red, worn smooth at the aisle corners.

Several tables are set for one or two people: heavy silverware, water glasses, folded napkins. One table near the middle holds a cup of black coffee still warm, a saucer with a curl of orange peel, and an open book facedown beside it. The book's cover is blank cloth. Its pages are printed in columns of dense text that remain legible only when not looked at directly.

At the far end, a narrow service counter contains a polished kettle, small cups, jars of tea, slices of dark cake beneath a glass dome, and a bowl of pears. No attendant appears. A handwritten card rests beside the kettle. Whatever language it uses, the meaning feels unusually easy: PLEASE LEAVE ENOUGH FOR THE NEXT PERSON.

Outside the windows, the train crosses a high viaduct. Far below, a valley is filled with scattered lights. For a few moments they form constellations against the ground, then the train curves and they become merely houses again.
places.name: the dining car at night

places.description:
Beyond the quieter glass door, the corridor narrows and the lamps dim to a soft amber. Compartment doors line one side, each with a small brass number plate. Most are closed. Several stand open just far enough to show made beds, folded blankets, washbasins, books left on shelves, and curtains drawn against the passing dark.

Compartment seven is fully open. Inside are two facing seats upholstered in blue wool, a small table beneath the window, and an upper berth folded neatly into the wall. Someone has left a coat hanging from the hook beside the door. It is dry, warm at the shoulders, and much too large to belong to anyone obvious.

On the table sits a paper cup containing three blackberries and a ticket punched with five irregular holes. The printed destination field is blank.

Farther down the corridor, one compartment has its light off but its curtain open. In the window, instead of the passing landscape, the reflection shows a sunlit platform crowded with travelers in summer clothes. The corridor behind you remains empty.
places.name: the sleeping compartments

places.description:
The warmer light at the end of the corridor comes from an observation car paneled almost entirely in glass. Curved windows wrap the rear and sides, framed by dark wood and brass. Low chairs face outward rather than inward. A small stove glows in one corner, giving the room a dry warmth and the faint smell of coal.

Here the train's motion becomes visible. The rails stream away behind in two silver lines before being swallowed by darkness. The landscape changes gradually and then all at once: forest gives way to open snowfield, snowfield to black rock under stars, black rock to a coast where moonlight lies across the sea like beaten metal.

On a narrow shelf beneath the rear window rests a stack of postcards. Each shows a different landscape the train has passed: a yellow desert under storm clouds, a city of white towers beside green water, an orchard in winter, a bridge crossing nothing but fog. None has writing on the back. One card at the bottom shows the observation car itself from outside, moving through a landscape of tall red grass under a sky with two moons.

The train has not yet passed that place.
places.name: the observation car

places.description:
A tall wooden door the color of old cedar, built from three broad vertical planks with grain that twists and rejoins over their length. There is no paint or varnish. The wood has been worn satin-smooth around a simple dark bronze handle.

The door is slightly taller than the frame seems to require. Its upper edge disappears into shadow between two amber lamps.

Near it, the lounge air occasionally carries a dry resinous scent mixed with damp earth. The bronze handle is neither warm nor cold. Very fine reddish fibers cling in one corner where the lowest plank meets the stone, too soft to be sawdust and too few to identify with confidence.
places.name: the cedar-colored door

places.description:
The air is cool, still, and scented with wet bark, sorrel, and dark soil. Great redwood trunks rise from the forest floor in every direction, some straight as columns, others widening into buttressed bases furred with moss. Their upper branches disappear into a high green dimness where sunlight breaks into moving shafts.

The ground is soft with centuries of needles and fallen leaves. Sword ferns spread shoulder-high in the hollows. Redwood sorrel carpets brighter patches in three-lobed green, folding slightly where droplets gather. A fallen branch as thick as a young tree lies half-buried in moss and has become its own small garden.

There is no single path. One faint route follows the land downhill where the sound of water comes and goes beneath birdsong. Another threads between two enormous trunks toward a fallen redwood whose root mass rises like a wall of earth and stone. Uphill, the forest opens just enough to show pale fog moving between the trees at a higher elevation.

Behind, the grove continues through close-set trunks and fern beds. Somewhere unseen, a woodpecker strikes three times and stops. Far overhead, something releases a brief shower of droplets that reaches the ground long after the branch that shed them has moved on.

The scale is not dramatic after a minute. It becomes ordinary. That may be the strangest part.
places.name: beyond

places.description:
The downhill route is barely a path at first, only a tendency in the ferns and a slight compression of the duff beneath them. The sound of water strengthens gradually until the ground levels into a narrow creek hollow shaded by alder, maple, and younger redwoods.

The creek is clear over dark stones, rarely more than knee-deep, moving in alternating runs and quiet amber pools. Fallen branches collect moss and leaf litter into small islands. In one place a redwood has fallen across the water and remained there long enough for huckleberry, fern, and two young trees to root along its upper surface.

The trunk makes a broad natural bridge. Upstream, the creek disappears around a bend under leaning trees where the air looks almost blue with shade. Downstream, sunlight flashes more strongly through the canopy and the water grows louder over stone.

On the far bank, a set of prints crosses a muddy patch and vanishes into sorrel. Four toes, no claw marks, larger than a fox and smaller than anything that ought to make the creek feel dangerous. They are fresh enough to hold a little water.
places.name: down where the creek runs

places.description:
The fallen redwood lies across a shallow hollow, its trunk broader than a room and its bark broken into long cinnamon-colored plates. The crown disappeared somewhere downslope long ago, but the base remains attached to a root mass that towers above the forest floor in a wall of dark soil, stone, and exposed roots.

Where the trunk split on impact, the interior has weathered into a dry chamber open along one side. It smells of old wood and dust instead of damp earth. Light enters through cracks in the fractured grain, making thin gold lines across the floor. A person could sit inside without stooping.

The root wall is full of pockets. Ferns grow from some; others hold stones polished smooth by soil movement. Near the lowest edge, a narrow passage continues behind the lifted roots into a cavity where the ground drops out of sight for several meters before leveling again.

Nothing about the place appears arranged, but tucked into one bark fissure is a feather almost as long as a forearm: barred grey and cream, clean, unbroken, and much larger than the birds heard in the grove.
places.name: at the fallen giant

places.description:
The uphill route steepens through sword ferns and exposed roots until the redwoods begin to stand farther apart. Fog moves visibly here, not as a blanket but in slow pale bands slipping between trunks and dissolving in pockets of sun.

The forest floor becomes rockier. Huckleberry gives way to low manzanita and patches of pale lichen. From one ledge, the grove drops away enough to reveal the tops of trees below, a green surface broken by taller crowns rising through it like islands.

The path continues along a narrow ridge where the wind finally reaches the ground. On the seaward side, fog occasionally thins enough to show a distant silver horizon far below. On the inland side, the land descends into another forested valley darker and denser than the one behind.

Near the highest point stands a redwood struck by lightning long ago. Its upper half is gone, but the hollow trunk remains alive around the edges, sending green branches from one side. Inside the blackened opening, warm air rises steadily from below, carrying a faint scent of stone after rain.
places.name: up into the fog

places.description:
A tall door of ribbed frosted glass held in a narrow frame of brushed metal. The glass is opaque except where light catches in its vertical grooves, producing soft bands that seem to move when viewed from the side. The handle is a simple horizontal bar, cool and almost weightless under the hand.

A faint film of condensation gathers occasionally along the lower pane, though the stone around it remains dry. The droplets do something mildly wrong: several creep upward before disappearing into the frame.

Close to the door, there is sometimes a smell of damp leaves, warm stone, citrus peel, and the metallic cleanliness of air after lightning.
places.name: the frosted glass door

places.description:
Warm white stone underfoot. High above, an immense curved roof of glass spans from horizon to horizon, crossed by slender ribs that catch the light. Beyond the glass is not weather but darkness: stars, a slow band of pale dust, and the blue-white crescent of a planet so large that its curvature fills much of the view.

The interior is a garden built at impossible scale. Terraces step downward through citrus trees, broad-leaved plants, palms, flowering vines, and shallow channels of clear water. The air is warm without being humid. Somewhere, hidden fans or vents move the leaves just enough to keep the place from feeling sealed.

Ahead, a long bridge of pale stone crosses above the lower gardens toward a grove bright with orange and gold fruit. To the left, broad stairs descend toward the sound of falling water and a cluster of low pools. To the right, a narrower path rises through dense ferns toward a high glass wall where the stars appear almost close enough to touch. Behind, a colonnade runs along the upper level through quiet seating alcoves and dark polished doors set between the columns.

There are no people in sight. Several chairs have been pulled slightly away from tables, as though recently used. A glass of water sits on a ledge with three beads of condensation sliding down its side.

Every few minutes, a faint tremor passes through the floor. The leaves barely move. The stars do.
places.name: departures:d5

places.description:
The pale bridge runs above two descending garden terraces, its parapets low enough to lean on. Below, narrow water channels divide beds of herbs, broad leaves, white flowers, and low trees trained along dark trellises. Warm air rises from the lower levels carrying rosemary, wet stone, and the sweet-bitter smell of citrus rind.

Ahead, the bridge enters a grove of small trees heavy with fruit in shades from deep green to orange-gold. Some resemble oranges or mandarins until seen closely: their skins are faintly translucent, and pale threads of light move slowly beneath the surface like veins.

The grove is arranged around a circular platform of dark wood. A long table stands there beneath hanging lamps, set with ceramic bowls and narrow glasses. Nothing is served except a shallow dish containing six pieces of fruit, each cut open to reveal a spiral of pearl-white segments around a dark red center.

From the platform, one path continues forward through the trees toward a brighter opening. Another turns right and climbs a narrow stair to a catwalk running just beneath the glass roof. A third slips left between hedges toward the sound of quiet conversation that stops whenever the leaves move.
places.name: departures:d5f

places.description:
The broad stairs descend between walls of glossy leaves until the garden opens around a series of low stone pools. Water moves continuously from one to the next over lips of black rock, producing a layered hush that masks nearly every other sound.

The pools are not decorative in any obvious sense. Some are warm enough to steam faintly. Others are cool and clear, filled with pale gravel and long translucent fish that flash blue when they turn. A narrow waterfall descends from a high channel in the wall into the lowest basin, where mist hangs just above the surface.

To the left, a path follows the pools downward beneath overhanging vines toward a dimmer level lit from below by strips of soft green light. Ahead, stepping stones cross the widest basin toward a small pavilion screened by hanging plants. To the right, a spiral stair rises around a column of flowing water, climbing toward the underside of the main terrace.

Near the lowest visible pool, a brass plaque is mounted flush with the stone. It contains no words, only a diagram of seven concentric circles. The smallest circle is filled in dark blue.
places.name: departures:d5l

places.description:
The right-hand path climbs gradually through ferns taller than a person, their fronds opening toward the glass wall. The higher it goes, the thinner the planting becomes until warm stone and low moss replace the dense garden.

Here the curved outer glass rises almost vertically. The planet beyond fills half the view: blue-white cloud systems turning over a dark ocean, lightning pulsing silently inside one distant storm. Stars remain visible above it despite the reflected interior light.

A row of low reclining chairs faces the glass. Between them stand small brass tables, each holding a different object beneath a clear cover: a smooth black stone, a dried seedpod, a folded scrap of silver fabric, a tiny mechanical bird with its wings closed.

Ahead, the path ends at a narrow balcony pressed against the glass. To the right, an iron stair climbs toward a maintenance level where the ribs of the roof can be reached. To the left, a passage slips behind a wall of tall bamboo into a darker section where the lighting changes from warm white to deep red.

Very far below the balcony, through several levels of garden and structure, a line of moving lights travels slowly around the interior circumference and disappears beneath the terraces.
places.name: departures:d5r

places.description:
The colonnade behind the arrival terrace runs along the upper edge of the garden beneath a lower ceiling of warm stone. Between the columns are deep seating alcoves with curved benches, woven rugs, low tables, and shelves holding books whose spines carry no titles.

Dark polished doors punctuate the inner wall. Most are closed. One stands open onto a quiet room with a long table and a ceiling painted midnight blue. Another reveals a short corridor lined with hooks and neatly folded robes. A third opens only a hand's width and emits air several degrees colder than the colonnade.

Farther back, the arcade bends left around the garden's curvature. Ahead, its lamps become fewer and the architecture older: pale stone gives way to darker blocks with visible tool marks. To the right, a short stair rises to a mezzanine overlooking the arrival terrace. To the left, a broad doorway opens into a chamber filled with low golden light and the smell of cedar smoke.

On one bench rests a small square card of thick cream paper. One side is blank. The other shows only a line drawing of the curved glass roof and, beneath it, seven small circles in a row. The fifth is marked with a dot.
places.name: departures:d5b

places.description:
The stair on the right is narrower than it first appears, its treads cut into the side of a pale structural rib. It climbs above the citrus canopy to a catwalk just beneath the glass roof, where the air is cooler and the garden below becomes a layered map of paths, pools, lights, and terraces.

The catwalk follows the curve of the roof. To one side is the immense interior garden; to the other, beyond the glass, the stars and the blue-white planet slide slowly across the field of view as the structure turns.

Small maintenance stations interrupt the walkway at intervals: folded ladders, sealed cabinets, brass gauges with needles moving too slowly to notice directly. One gauge is labeled only by seven colored arcs. Its needle rests in the fifth.

Ahead, the catwalk reaches a junction where one branch continues along the roof toward a bank of darker glass. Another rises by a short ladder to a tiny exterior-looking platform enclosed entirely in clear panels. From below, someone has placed a single chair there facing the planet.

Far beneath, the circular table in the citrus grove appears occupied for several seconds by three dark figures. When looked at again, the chairs are empty.
places.name: departures:d5fr

places.description:
The left-hand path follows the pools downward beneath curtains of vine until the warm garden light fades behind. The lower level is cooler, lit by narrow green strips set into the floor and by the water itself, which carries a faint blue glow along the edges of each basin.

The architecture becomes more utilitarian here: dark stone, metal grilles, exposed channels carrying water from one terrace to another. Yet somebody has placed benches wherever the passages widen, and small flowering plants grow from cracks that seem too deliberate to be accidental.

Ahead, the path reaches a chamber where seven vertical sheets of water fall from ceiling to floor in parallel, each entering a separate black basin. The fifth sheet is slightly warmer than the others. Behind it, visible only when the flow thins for a moment, is a narrow opening in the wall.

To the right, a grated walkway follows the waterworks toward a low mechanical hum. To the left, a set of shallow steps continues still farther down into blue darkness where the air smells faintly of rain and iron.
places.name: departures:d5ld

places.description:
The iron stair on the right climbs through a hatch into the narrow space between the garden and the roof structure. Up here the white stone disappears. Everything is steel ribs, cable runs, glass supports, and slim maintenance walkways with open grating underfoot.

The garden spreads below through the gaps, warm and green. Above and beside the walkway, the curved glass is close enough to show tiny imperfections in its surface: faint scratches, embedded bubbles, a dusting of frost along one seam. Beyond it, the planet fills the view so completely that the horizon is no longer visible.

Ahead, the walkway follows the roof toward a cluster of equipment housings. To the left, a short bridge crosses to another structural rib. To the right, there is nowhere to go except the glass.

At the nearest junction stands a waist-high metal box with a hinged cover. Inside are seven identical brass keys hanging from hooks. Six are dull with age. The fifth is bright from recent handling.

A narrow label beneath them contains a single line of local script. Unlike the garden signage, this one settles almost immediately into meaning: EMERGENCY ACCESS — DO NOT REMOVE ALL SEVEN.
places.name: departures:d5ru

places.description:
Passing through the fifth sheet of falling water is less dramatic than it looks. The flow parts around shoulders and closes again behind, warm enough to feel like summer rain. Beyond it is a narrow stone corridor lit only by reflections from the basin outside.

The passage runs straight for perhaps thirty paces, then opens into a circular chamber hollowed into darker rock. In the center stands a shallow round reservoir no wider than a dining table. Its water is perfectly still and nearly black. Six narrow channels enter it at equal intervals around the wall. A seventh channel, directly opposite the entrance, is dry.

Set into the wall above that dry channel is a small brass door with no visible hinge. It has seven round depressions arranged in an arc. The fifth contains a tiny bead of blue glass.

Nothing happens when the room is entered. Nothing hums. Nothing lights. Water from the six active channels simply continues to feed the central pool without raising its level.

To the left, a maintenance passage follows one of the wet channels into darkness. To the right, a narrow stair climbs behind the chamber wall. Ahead, beneath the brass panel and the dry seventh channel, the stone floor slopes very slightly downward toward a seam too straight to be geological.
places.name: departures:d5ldf

places.description:
The short ladder ends inside a clear enclosure no larger than a small balcony. Glass surrounds it on every side except the floor. The single chair is fixed to the deck and faces outward toward the blue-white planet.

From here, the garden below is almost entirely hidden by the curvature of the roof. The view becomes space, glass, and the enormous turning weather of the world outside. Lightning blooms silently across a storm system the size of a continent. Along the night side, faint threads of gold suggest cities or fires or something else arranged along coastlines.

A narrow console beside the chair holds seven mechanical switches beneath seven indicator windows. Six windows are dark. The fifth glows a steady amber. None of the switches is labeled.

Beside the console is a shallow recess containing a pair of optical lenses in a folding brass frame. Through them, the planet's night side becomes sharper. For several seconds, among the golden lines below, one tiny pattern seems unmistakably to resemble the curved roof of the garden itself.

Then cloud covers it.

There is nowhere else to walk from the enclosure. The only path is back down the ladder.
places.name: departures:d5fru

places.description:
A red-painted wooden door with a narrow brass push plate and a small rectangular slot near eye level. The paint has faded unevenly around the edges, revealing older layers of cream and blue beneath. A tiny round bulb above the frame is dark.

The lower half of the door is scuffed as though by shoes, carts, or impatient weather. The brass plate is warm to the touch.

Now and then, standing close, there is a smell of salt air, hot sugar, machine oil, and something fried in batter. Very faintly, from nowhere that can be located, comes a sequence of three bright musical notes followed by a soft mechanical clunk.
places.name: the red-painted door

places.description:
A boardwalk stretches beneath a deep blue evening sky, the horizon still holding a last band of copper light over a dark sea. Strings of bulbs run from pole to pole, reflected in wet planks and polished metal. Somewhere farther along, a carousel organ plays a tune just slowly enough to sound unfamiliar.

Ahead, the boardwalk continues between shuttered food stalls, game booths, and glowing signs toward a tall wheel turning steadily against the sky. To the left, an open arcade spills colored light across the boards beneath a striped awning. To the right, a wide pier branches over the water toward a pavilion hung with lanterns. Behind, a narrower promenade follows the seawall past benches, telescopes, and a row of small painted kiosks.

Nothing appears closed, exactly. A fryer hisses behind one counter. A rack of paper cups is full. Rows of plush prizes stare down from a game stall with extraordinary confidence in their own value. The rides move. The lights work. No attendant is visible.

The air smells of salt, hot sugar, popcorn, ozone, and old wood. Gulls call somewhere beyond the lamps. Every few minutes, the tall wheel stops with one car at the very top, waits for several seconds, then begins turning again.
places.name: departures:d6

places.description:
The boardwalk broadens as it approaches the tall wheel. Game stalls line one side: rings tossed over glass bottles, a row of painted ducks circling slowly in a tin channel, three wooden targets that fold backward when struck. The prize shelves are crowded with improbable animals in bright fabric, none corresponding very closely to any known species.

On the other side, food counters glow beneath enamel signs. Paper cones of sugared nuts sit beneath warm lamps. A machine turns glossy red apples through a curtain of caramel. Behind one counter, a metal basket rises from oil by itself, drains for ten seconds, then descends empty again.

The wheel ahead turns with a low electric hum. Its cars are enclosed in glass and painted cream. At ground level, one door stands open whenever the wheel stops. No barrier prevents boarding.

Just before the wheel, a narrow path continues forward toward a darker section of the boardwalk where the lights become sparse and the sea seems louder. To the right, steps lead up to the wheel platform. To the left, a brightly lit game booth bears a sign consisting only of a painted gold star with one point missing.
places.name: departures:d6f

places.description:
The arcade is warmer than the boardwalk and loud in a hundred small ways. Rows of cabinets blink beneath a striped ceiling: mechanical races, ball games, claw machines, shooting galleries, fortune wheels, tiny theaters that animate when a coin is inserted. Most controls are familiar enough to invite use even when the rules are not.

A change machine near the entrance dispenses small brass tokens with a gull stamped on one side and a blank circle on the other. A shallow tray beneath it already holds nine.

Farther in, the games become older. Painted wooden cabinets replace glass and chrome. One machine offers to test strength with a padded mallet. Another contains a miniature seaside town under glass; when its brass lever is pulled, tiny lights come on one building at a time while a model storm rolls in from painted clouds.

Ahead, the arcade narrows toward a curtain of dark blue beads and a sign showing an eye inside a shell. To the left, a side room contains rows of pinball tables whose backglasses depict places that look suspiciously like real landscapes rather than game art. To the right, an open doorway leads into a room of mirrors lit by slow-changing bulbs.

Somewhere among the machines, a bell rings whenever nobody is touching anything.
places.name: departures:d6l

places.description:
The pier extends over dark water on heavy timber pilings, lanterns strung between tall posts. The boardwalk here is wider and less crowded with machinery. Wooden benches face the sea. Fishing rods rest unattended against the rail, their lines disappearing into black water that occasionally flashes green with small drifting lights.

At the end stands an octagonal pavilion with open sides and a copper roof. Inside are tables, a small bandstand, and strings of paper lanterns painted with waves, moons, and silver fish. A record player sits on a cabinet beside the bandstand, turning slowly with no record on its platter.

To the left, a narrow stair descends to a lower landing just above the water. To the right, a side pier reaches toward a cluster of floating lanterns tethered beyond the main structure. Ahead, through the pavilion, a short bridge connects to a smaller platform where one telescope points not toward the sky but straight down into the sea.

From somewhere beneath the pier comes a low resonant sound like a glass rim being rubbed by a wet finger. It repeats at irregular intervals, never quite the same pitch twice.
places.name: departures:d6r

places.description:
The promenade behind the arrival point follows the seawall beneath a row of low lamps with frosted globes. The boardwalk noise softens here. Benches face the water, separated by coin-operated telescopes and small painted kiosks with shutters propped open.

One kiosk sells postcards depicting the boardwalk in different weather: blazing noon, winter fog, heavy rain, snow piled against the arcade, a green sky over an empty sea. None shows the deep blue evening that actually surrounds it.

Farther along, the seawall curves toward a small stone pavilion with a domed roof and open arches. Beyond that, the lights become sparse and the promenade enters a strip of wind-bent grass between the sea and a dark line of low houses.

To the left, steps climb to a terrace above the boardwalk where strings of unlit bulbs hang between poles. To the right, a gate in the seawall stands open onto a narrow stair descending toward the rocks at water level. Ahead, the promenade continues past the pavilion into quieter ground.

Pinned beneath the glass of one postcard rack is a handwritten note in blue ink: BEST VIEW AFTER THE LIGHTS GO OUT.
places.name: departures:d6b

places.description:
The steps rise to a narrow loading platform beside the wheel. A cream-painted car settles into place with a soft pneumatic sigh and its glass door folds open. Inside are two padded benches, a brass handrail, and a small round table bolted between them. There are no controls.

Once aboard, the wheel carries the car upward with almost insulting gentleness. The boardwalk shrinks below into lines of bulbs and colored rectangles. The sea widens. At halfway height, the coast becomes visible in both directions, curving farther than expected beneath the blue evening.

Near the top, the music from below fades completely. When the wheel reaches its highest point, it stops.

For several seconds the entire amusement pier goes dark.

The sea does not. Thousands of pale green lights are moving beneath the surface in long slow bands, far beyond the pier and all along the coast. They are too coordinated to be reflections and too numerous to be boats. From above, several bands curve into enormous loops before dissolving.

Then the boardwalk lights return, the wheel starts again, and the green patterns become almost impossible to see from the descending car.
places.name: departures:d6fr

places.description:
The dark blue bead curtain opens into a booth scarcely larger than a closet. Its walls are lined with tiny drawers, each fitted with a brass pull and a number plate. A single chair faces a round table beneath a hanging lamp.

On the table sits a mechanical shell mounted on a black base. Its pearly interior contains a small glass eye. A slot beside it accepts one of the arcade's brass gull tokens.

When a token drops in, the eye closes. The shell turns once with a series of delicate clicks. Then one drawer somewhere in the wall opens by itself.

The drawer contains no fortune slip. It holds a small ordinary object: a red thread, a button, a dried leaf, a key blank, a piece of chalk, a blue marble. Which drawer opens is impossible to predict.

A handwritten card beside the machine reads: TAKE IT IF YOU NEED IT. PUT SOMETHING BACK IF YOU DON'T.

Below that, in smaller writing: THE SHELL HAS NEVER EXPLAINED ITSELF AND WE HAVE STOPPED ASKING.
places.name: departures:d6lf

places.description:
The short bridge ends at a circular platform barely wider than the brass telescope fixed to its center. Unlike the coin-operated instruments along the seawall, this one has no eyepiece cap, no payment slot, and no mechanism for changing direction. It points straight down between the pilings into the dark sea.

Through the glass, surface reflection disappears. The water becomes transparent far beyond what ordinary depth should allow. Small green lights drift past like sparks. Schools of silver fish turn together beneath them. Lower still, the timber pilings vanish into blue-black distance.

Then the bottom appears.

It is not sand. A broad pale surface crosses the field of view, curved and marked by long parallel grooves. At first it resembles stone. Then a line of darker circles passes beneath the lens at perfectly even intervals, each one wider than the telescope's entire view.

Whatever the structure is, the pier has been built directly above it.

Scratched into the brass housing are four words in plain block letters: DO NOT DROP COINS HERE.
places.name: departures:d6rf

places.description:
Past the stone pavilion, the promenade leaves the brightest part of the boardwalk behind. The lamps stand farther apart. Wind-bent grass grows between the paving stones and the seawall lowers until the dark water is visible without leaning over it.

The line of low houses begins here: narrow fronts painted cream, blue, and faded yellow, each with a tiny porch facing the sea. Most windows are dark. One porch light burns above an empty rocking chair. Another house has a radio playing softly somewhere inside, too muffled to make out words.

Farther ahead, the promenade ends at a broad grassy point overlooking the water. A wooden bench sits there beneath no lamp at all.

As the last boardwalk lights behind finally click off in sequence, the sky seems to brighten by comparison. The sea answers a moment later. Pale green bands appear beneath the surface, first near shore and then farther out, curving through the darkness like slow handwriting.

From the bench, the pattern is larger than it looked from the wheel. Several lines converge offshore around a single dark patch where no light passes at all.

Nothing arrives. Nothing emerges. The show is simply there, and then, after several minutes, it fades.
places.name: departures:d6bf

places.description:
A plain door painted warm white, with a black iron latch and a narrow strip of frosted glass above eye level. The enamel is chipped along one lower corner and slightly yellowed around the hinges. Nothing about it looks grand enough to belong beside the stranger doors.

The latch is cool. The upper glass carries a shifting pearly brightness with no visible source.

Standing near it, the air sometimes smells faintly of woodsmoke, wool, baked bread, and the dry mineral cold that clings to clothing after snow. Once in a while there is a soft tick from the other side, followed several seconds later by another, as though a hot stove were contracting.
places.name: the white enamel door

places.description:
A low room glows with firelight and the pale reflection of snow through broad windows. Thick timber beams cross the ceiling. A black iron stove ticks softly beside a stone hearth, and a kettle gives off the faintest thread of steam.

A long wooden table stands beneath the windows with two mismatched chairs and a loaf of dark bread under a linen cloth. Beside it are a crock of salted butter, a bowl of apples, and a pot of something savory cooling beneath a lid. Wool blankets are folded over the back of a bench. Wet mittens hang from pegs near an archway.

Outside, snow falls steadily over a small valley. Spruce trees climb the opposite slope. A frozen lake lies below the house, pale beneath the storm, with one line of dark open water near the far shore. No road is visible.

Ahead, a short hall leads deeper into the house toward a stair and several small rooms. To the left, glass doors open onto a covered porch facing the lake. To the right, a tiled passage leads toward a bath room where warm mist clouds the windows. Behind, an open kitchen occupies the other half of the main room, its shelves stocked and its brick oven still hot.

The clock above the stove has stopped at 4:17. The kettle has not.
places.name: departures:d7

places.description:
The covered porch runs the length of the house beneath a steep roof loaded with snow. A row of hooks holds two lanterns, a coil of rope, and a pair of wooden snowshoes. Three broad chairs face the valley with thick wool pads tied to their seats.

The cold outside is sharp but not cruel. Snow falls in large dry flakes that make almost no sound when they strike the porch rail. The frozen lake below reflects the pale sky, except for that narrow line of open water along the far shore where mist rises in slow ribbons.

Steps descend from the porch into knee-deep snow. To the left, a line of half-buried stones leads toward a small shed and a stand of spruce. Ahead, a faint path slopes directly toward the lake, marked by occasional poles tied with red cloth. To the right, the porch wraps around the house toward a woodpile and a low detached building with steam issuing from a metal chimney.

On the railing rests a ceramic mug. Its contents have frozen solid. A tiny evergreen needle is trapped in the ice.
places.name: departures:d7l

places.description:
The tiled passage ends in a bathing room built partly into the stone foundation. Warm mist fogs the lower halves of the windows. A rectangular pool occupies most of the floor, fed by a narrow channel of clear hot water running from the wall.

The room is simple: pale tile, dark wood benches, hooks for towels, a shelf holding soap that smells faintly of pine and citrus. The pool is deep enough to sit in comfortably, with a submerged stone ledge along one side. Snow can be seen accumulating outside through the upper glass while the water remains almost too warm.

To the right, a small door opens into a dry sauna lined with cedar. Ahead, another glass door leads to an exterior stone terrace where a round hot pool steams beneath falling snow. To the left, a narrow passage slopes downward alongside the hot-water channel toward the source.

Someone has drawn a tiny fish in the condensation on one window. Beneath it, with one finger: TOO HOT TODAY.
places.name: departures:d7r

places.description:
The short hall is warmer than the main room, lined with framed charcoal sketches of mountains, trees, and one stubbornly ordinary loaf of bread. A staircase rises beneath a small window where snow has gathered along the outer sill.

Upstairs are three compact bedrooms beneath the sloping roof and a narrow landing furnished with a bookcase and a chair. Each room is made up differently: one with a heavy blue quilt, one with layered wool blankets in red and brown, one with white linen and a small writing desk beneath the eaves.

The blue room faces the lake. The red room looks toward the spruce slope. The white room has a skylight almost entirely covered by snow except for one clear oval where something warm beneath the glass has kept it from settling.

At the end of the landing, a steep ladder continues up toward a square ceiling hatch. A faint current of cold air comes down around its edges.

On the writing desk in the white room is a stack of blank paper and a sharpened pencil. The top sheet bears only a date with no year: 17 January.
places.name: departures:d7f

places.description:
The kitchen occupies the back half of the main room beneath lower beams darkened by years of smoke. Open shelves hold crockery, jars of grain, dried mushrooms, onions, tea tins, salt, sugar, and more spices than the rest of the house seems ambitious enough to require.

The brick oven is still hot. A round loaf cools on a wooden board beside it. Copper pots hang above a deep stone sink, and a heavy kettle simmers on the iron range. Nothing is actively cooking, but several things look recently finished: a pot of root-vegetable stew, roasted apples glazed with something dark, a tray of small seed rolls.

To the left, a narrow pantry descends three steps into a cool room lined with shelves. Ahead, a back window looks directly into the falling snow and the spruce woods beyond. To the right, a short passage leads toward the woodpile and the detached steaming building glimpsed from the porch.

A handwritten card has been tucked into the flour jar lid: IF YOU FINISH THE BREAD, START ANOTHER. NO ONE LIKES THE LAST SLICE AS MUCH AS THEY CLAIM.
places.name: departures:d7b

places.description:
The path from the porch descends through deep snow toward the lake, marked every dozen paces by slender poles tied with faded red cloth. In the open valley the wind becomes more noticeable, pushing loose powder in thin ribbons across the crust.

At the shore, the ice begins beneath a shelf of snow and extends pale and matte toward the far bank. Fine cracks branch beneath the surface like dark threads trapped in milk glass. The line of open water seen from the house lies far across the lake, steaming faintly beneath the falling snow.

A narrow wooden dock projects twenty paces onto the ice before ending at a small roofed shelter. Beneath its bench are several pairs of old skates in different sizes and a long pole with a metal hook. A hand-painted board reads CHECK THE ICE YOURSELF. THE LAKE HAS NO OPINION ABOUT YOUR CONFIDENCE.

To the right, a line of footprints follows the shoreline toward a stand of spruce where the bank becomes rocky. Ahead, a sequence of dark wooden stakes crosses partway over the ice toward a tiny island scarcely visible through the snowfall. To the left, the shore curves beneath a steep white slope where several dark openings show between boulders.

Something moves once in the open water at the far side. The distance is too great to tell whether it was an animal, current, or falling snow playing tricks with scale.
places.name: departures:d7lf

places.description:
A heavy-looking iron door made from overlapping dark plates, each fixed with round rivets. The surface is matte except where the edge of a recessed handle has been worn smooth. No rust marks the metal.

The door is unexpectedly warm near the bottom and cool near the top. Fine droplets occasionally gather along one vertical seam and vanish before reaching the floor.

Close to the seam, the air carries the damp mineral smell of warm water over stone, with a trace of salt. A faint sweeter scent comes and goes, somewhere between crushed basil and rain on hot pavement. If the room is very quiet, a distant low sound can sometimes be heard through the metal—not surf exactly, but something large moving water.
places.name: the black iron door

places.description:
The passage opens onto a black-sand shore beneath a cavern so vast that its ceiling disappears into darkness. There is no sky. Instead, thousands of pale blue-green lights burn far overhead in irregular constellations: mineral veins, colonies of tiny luminous growths, and slow drifting points that may be insects or something similar at impossible distance.

A warm underground sea fills most of the cavern. Its surface is almost black except where the overhead lights break into long trembling reflections. Small waves arrive quietly on the shore, leaving narrow lines of phosphorescence that fade after several seconds.

Ahead, a low wooden jetty extends into the water toward three narrow boats tied beneath a lamp. To the left, the beach curves along the cavern wall where enormous pale fungi rise between boulders and release faintly glowing spores when disturbed by air currents. To the right, stone steps climb toward a series of terraces cut into the cliff, some holding steaming pools. Behind, a river emerges from a dark arch in the rock and spreads shallowly across the sand before joining the sea.

The air is warm enough for bare arms and smells of salt, stone, wet wood, and green things growing without sunlight.

Far across the water, beyond the reach of any ordinary lamp, a line of gold lights marks something on the opposite shore.
places.name: departures:d8

places.description:
The jetty is made from dark timber polished by moisture and use. Its lamp burns with a steady yellow flame inside thick glass. Three narrow boats are tied along the outer edge, each built from pale wood and fitted with two oars, a folded blanket, and a small covered lantern.

The water beside the dock is clear enough to show silver fish moving between the pilings. Farther out it becomes black almost immediately.

One boat contains a shallow wooden box holding a coil of rope, a tin cup, and a hand-drawn chart on waterproof cloth. The chart shows the near shore, several low islands, a deep-water route toward the distant gold lights, and one large blank area crossed out with three parallel strokes.

Ahead lies open water. To the left, a chain of low rocky islets breaks the surface beneath clusters of blue-green ceiling light. To the right, the cavern wall curves out of sight behind a dark headland. Far ahead, the gold lights remain steady and evenly spaced.

Every so often something large passes beneath the jetty without surfacing. The fish scatter, then return.
places.name: departures:d8f

places.description:
The beach curves left beneath the cavern wall into a grove of enormous pale fungi. Some rise taller than houses on thick ribbed stalks, their caps translucent at the edges and faintly blue from within. Smaller growths cluster around their bases in shelves, cups, and branching forms that resemble coral.

The ground changes from black sand to springy dark soil veined with white threads. Each footstep releases a soft earthy smell. When air moves through the grove, fine luminous spores drift from the largest caps and settle slowly like greenish snow.

Ahead, the grove thickens around a low ridge of stone. To the left, a narrow path follows the cavern wall toward a region where the fungi become red and amber instead of blue. To the right, several fallen caps form broad natural platforms overlooking the underground sea.

Near the ridge, a cluster of small bell-shaped fungi gives off distinct musical tones when drops of condensation strike them. The notes are irregular but not random enough to ignore comfortably.

A line of tiny footprints crosses the soil beneath them and disappears under one of the largest stalks.
places.name: departures:d8l

places.description:
The stone steps climb above the black beach through warm mist. They lead to a series of terraces carved into the cavern wall, each holding a shallow pool fed by clear mineral water seeping from narrow channels in the rock.

The lowest pools are almost body-warm and edged with dark stone benches. Higher ones grow hotter, steaming in the cavern air. Mineral deposits have built pale rims around them in cream, rose, and faint green, making the terraces look half natural and half deliberately tended.

To the right, the stairs continue upward toward a narrow overlook above the sea. Ahead, a long rectangular pool extends beneath an overhang where drops of cold water fall from the ceiling into the steam. To the left, a short passage enters the rock beside the hottest pool.

Someone has stacked six smooth black stones beside one basin. A seventh lies alone several feet away near the edge of the terrace.

From this height, the distant gold lights across the underground sea appear to form a straight line far too precise to be campfires.
places.name: departures:d8r

places.description:
The shallow river behind the arrival shore is warm at the ankles and clear over black pebbles. It emerges from a broad arch in the cavern wall, carrying bits of pale leaf, tiny translucent shrimp, and occasional ribbons of green light that dissolve when lifted from the water.

Following it upstream, the ceiling lowers gradually until the immense sea cavern is hidden behind bends in the rock. The air becomes wetter and more fragrant. Moss thickens along the banks. Small ferns grow from cracks wherever mineral-rich water drips.

Ahead, the river divides around a stone island supporting a single enormous tree with white bark and dark glossy leaves. Its roots enter the water on all sides. To the left, the deeper branch flows beneath hanging roots toward a chamber lit amber from somewhere unseen. To the right, a narrower channel remains shallow enough to wade and disappears around a wall of mossy stone.

The tree bears no fruit, but several branches hold empty woven baskets suspended by cords. One basket contains a folded dry towel.

Farther upstream, beyond the island, something knocks twice against wood and then waits.
places.name: departures:d8b

places.description:
A broad wooden door washed in faded ochre, its surface matte and dusty-looking even in the damp air of the lounge. A narrow iron handle sits low on the right. Near the bottom, the paint has darkened in irregular shapes like rain once struck it and dried there.

The wood feels warm. If a hand rests on it long enough, the air close to the threshold seems drier, carrying faint traces of desert dust, damp stone, creosote, and the sharp metallic smell that sometimes comes before a storm.

A thin line of reddish grit sometimes appears along the threshold and is gone the next time anyone looks.
places.name: the ochre door

places.description:
The air is warm and newly washed. A high desert spreads under enormous retreating storm clouds, the ground darkened by rain and fragrant with wet dust, sage, and creosote. Far mesas burn copper where late sunlight breaks through beneath the cloud shelf.

A shallow sheet of water has gathered across part of the plain, turning the desert into a temporary mirror. Lightning flickers silently inside the storm moving away to the east. The temperature is dropping by the minute.

Ahead, a broad wash carries a thin stream toward a gap between red cliffs. To the left, low black hills rise from fields of pale grass and scattered stone. To the right, a sandstone shelf slopes upward toward a line of weather-twisted juniper and a distant overlook. Behind, the land falls almost imperceptibly toward a wide basin where rainwater has collected in bright temporary pools.

There are no roads or buildings. Tireless small frogs have somehow already begun calling from water that did not exist an hour ago.

On the western horizon, the sun drops through a clear band beneath the clouds and turns every wet surface briefly gold.
places.name: departures:d9

places.description:
The wash is broad and shallow, its sandy floor darkened by runoff. A thin ribbon of water winds through it, no more than ankle-deep in most places, carrying twigs, foam, and the occasional bright leaf between banks cut smooth by older floods.

The red cliffs ahead draw closer until the wash narrows into a canyon mouth. Water has darkened the lower rock almost purple, while the upper walls glow orange in the last sunlight. The smell of wet sandstone is stronger here.

Ahead, the canyon bends out of sight around a tall fin of rock. To the left, a sloping ledge rises above the wash toward several shallow alcoves in the cliff face. To the right, a side channel enters from a narrower cleft where fresh runoff still trickles down stepped stone.

High on one wall, well above any recent water line, a row of small dark handprints appears beneath an overhang. They are too far up to reach from the wash floor without climbing.
places.name: departures:d9f

places.description:
The black hills are lower than they first appeared but steeper underfoot, built from broken volcanic stone that gives a little with each step. Rain has collected in every hollow, turning the dark rock glossy and making small temporary streams between clumps of pale grass.

From the first ridge, the desert opens behind in bands of wet red earth and reflected sky. The retreating storm is now farther east, its underside flickering violet over distant country.

Ahead, the ridge continues toward a cluster of larger basalt outcrops. To the left, a shallow saddle drops into a hidden bowl where several temporary pools have formed among wildflowers flattened by rain. To the right, a rough descent leads toward a field of tall narrow stones standing upright in no obvious pattern.

One of the upright stones has a shallow circular depression in its top holding rainwater. A small green beetle swims around the edge as if this has always been a pond.
places.name: departures:d9l

places.description:
The sandstone shelf rises in broad natural steps warmed by the departing sun. Rainwater runs from higher ledges in silver threads and gathers in potholes filled with reflected cloud. Junipers lean away from the prevailing wind, their dark branches bright with droplets.

The climb is easy until the shelf narrows near the rim of a shallow escarpment. From there the overlook reveals country hidden from the arrival plain: layered mesas, braided washes, and a distant salt flat reflecting the storm like a second sky.

Ahead, the shelf continues along the rim toward a solitary stone arch. To the right, a steeper route climbs toward a rounded summit marked by one lightning-struck juniper. To the left, a shallow ravine descends through slickrock toward a cluster of cottonwoods improbably green against the red earth.

Near the overlook, a rectangular patch of sandstone is darker than the rest, protected from weather by something that is no longer there.
places.name: departures:d9r

places.description:
The land behind slopes so gently that the change is visible only when the arrival plain disappears from view. Rainwater has gathered here in a chain of temporary basins divided by low ridges of clay and grass. Some are only inches deep; others reflect the clouds so perfectly they seem cut through the earth.

The frog calls are louder here. Tiny dark bodies move at the edges of the pools. White moths rise from damp grass in sudden clouds and settle again. The storm wind has dropped almost completely.

Ahead, the basin continues toward a broad shallow lake that may not exist by tomorrow. To the left, a line of low dunes separates the pools from a field of flowering desert plants. To the right, the ground rises toward a broken fence of naturally standing stone slabs.

Near the largest pool, rain has exposed a pale spiral object half-buried in the mud, larger than a dinner plate and ridged like a shell. It is stone, not bone, and much older than the water around it.
places.name: departures:d9b

places.description:
A pair of narrow brass elevator doors set directly into the limestone wall, their surfaces softly tarnished except where countless imagined hands might have polished the edges. Above them is a semicircular indicator with no numbers, only a single black needle resting slightly left of center.

There is one round call button in a porcelain mount. It does not light when pressed. The doors sometimes give off a faint warmth, followed by the muted vibration of machinery moving somewhere impossibly far above or below.

Very close to the seam, the air carries faint smells of beeswax, old carpet, polished wood, coffee, and salt air.
places.name: the brass elevator doors

places.description:
The doors open onto the upper lobby of an old hotel built into a sea cliff. Tall arched windows occupy the entire outer wall, revealing an ocean hundreds of feet below and a horizon washed pale by late afternoon. Waves strike the cliff in white bursts so far beneath that their sound arrives softened and delayed.

The lobby is high-ceilinged and quiet, with patterned rugs, dark wood paneling, brass lamps, potted palms, and deep chairs arranged around low tables. A broad staircase descends through the center toward lower terraces. A cage elevator of polished wood and brass rises through the opposite wall, its indicator moving slowly between floors with no visible passengers.

Ahead, glass doors open onto a wide terrace cantilevered above the sea. To the left, a long gallery leads past reading rooms and a library whose windows face inland toward mountains. To the right, a tiled corridor curves toward the sound of water and a faint scent of chlorine and eucalyptus. Behind, the lobby continues through an archway into a dining room and bar where white tablecloths are already laid for evening.

At the reception desk, an open guest book contains names in many hands. Every room number is legible. Every guest name has faded just enough to resist reading.
places.name: departures:d10

places.description:
The sea terrace extends beyond the lobby windows on pale stone supports hidden somewhere below the cliff edge. Low walls are topped with warm metal rails. Deep chairs and small round tables face outward beneath striped canvas awnings that stir in the breeze.

The ocean dominates everything. From this height, individual waves become moving lines of white, and the cliff casts a dark wedge over water nearer the hotel. Far offshore, a small island rises from the haze with a lighthouse or tower at its highest point.

Ahead, the terrace narrows into a walkway following the cliff face toward a glass pavilion. To the left, broad steps descend to a lower sun deck planted with rosemary and lavender. To the right, a narrow balcony wraps around the hotel's outer wall toward a corner where several windows stand open.

On one table sits a silver tray with a sweating glass of pale sparkling water, two slices of lemon, and an unopened envelope addressed only: FOR THE GUEST WHO CAME OUTSIDE.
places.name: departures:d10f

places.description:
The gallery on the left is carpeted in a deep faded red and lined with tall windows on one side, framed landscapes and old maps on the other. The maps disagree subtly about the coastline outside.

Several reading rooms open from the gallery, each furnished differently: green leather chairs and newspapers in one, low sofas and chessboards in another, narrow writing desks beneath lamps in a third. At the far end, double doors stand open into a library two stories high.

Ahead, the library's central aisle runs toward a bay window overlooking distant mountains streaked with snow. To the left, a spiral stair climbs to the upper shelves and a mezzanine bridge. To the right, a smaller room contains travel books, atlases, and shelves of guidebooks with their destination names rubbed away.

One atlas lies open on a table. The page shows a coastline resembling the one below the hotel, but the hotel itself is absent. In the margin, somebody has penciled: BETTER THIS WAY.
places.name: departures:d10l

places.description:
